objective: For the fixed p=2,q=2 atom on r=3^k cores, construct a globally reselected aggregate Q witness with bounded capacity defect and a one-time aggregate edge-coloring repair to actual leaf matchings; isolate the iteration invariant without claiming the growing-budget face.

atomic_claims.text: For every k>=2, r=3^k, p=q=2 and every actual short set of size 3<=a<=r, explicit boundary formulas plus the C28 interval inequalities give a saturated primal matching the all-one-third dual L=(C(r,2)+2a+2r)/3.
A complete reselection using two affine parallel classes yields a Q-feasible point with S_core=S_long=0 and S_short=2(a mod3), hence L-Q<=4/3, without freezing old support.

For an integral aggregate leaf resource graph H, deleting R so chi'(H-R)<=m converts it to m actual leaf matchings with objective loss exactly |R|; the repair is paid once for the aggregate graph, not once per leaf.

For p=q=2 the aggregate short and long graphs are triangle factors; deleting one edge per component and two-coloring the resulting paths gives an actual host packing with total capacity defect r+a+(a mod3)<=2r+2, so nu_star-nu<=(2r+2)/3 on this slice.

Generator-side exact checks cover all 111 cardinality cases at r=9,27,81, all 466 actual nine-core subsets of size at least three, complete nine-core matching witnesses, and boundary controls; finite checks do not prove the universal theorem.
